title: "Design in Practice" by Rich Hickey

why_hn: HN draws on it for practical decision-making and problem-framing techniques that apply well beyond Clojure.

title: God Mode (Person of Interest)(2 x 22)

title: BigDog Overview (Updated March 2010)

title: Inside a heated shower head.  (suicide shower)

title: Dutch Cities are Better for the Environment (and my sanity)

title: Balaji Srinivasan at Startup School 2013

title: BeOS Demo Video

title: Red Bead Experiment with Dr. W. Edwards Deming
summary: Excerpts from W. Edwards Deming's Red Bead Experiment, where workers draw beads from a bowl and are judged on red ones that are largely down to chance. It shows how system variation, not individual effort, drives results.
why_hn: HN cites it as a classic illustration of dysfunctional management, gamed targets, and blaming workers for systemic outcomes.

title: The Nuclear Salt Water Rocket - Possibly the Craziest Rocket Engine Ever Imagined.

title: Your toothbrush is worn-out!

why_hn: HN commenters link it for electron micrographs of fresh versus worn bristles when toothbrush wear comes up.

title: Elon Musk: Tesla Autopilot | Lex Fridman Podcast #18

title: Andy Matuschak — The reason most learning tools fail

title: † Carpenter Brut † TURBO KILLER † Directed by Seth Ickerman † Official Video †
summary: The official video for Carpenter Brut's Turbo Killer, directed by Seth Ickerman, with psychedelic 1980s-styled visuals set to rock-leaning synthwave.

title: dotJS 2012 - Brian Leroux - WTFJS
summary: Brian Leroux's dotJS 2012 talk WTFJS is a quick, humorous tour of JavaScript's odd behaviors and quirks.
why_hn: Linked as a funny tour of JavaScript gotchas, usually to show the language has oddities of its own.

title: Autechre - Gantz Graf (Official Music Video) 1080p HD
summary: The official music video for Autechre's 'Gantz Graf', a dense, glitchy electronic track paired with abstract animated 3D visuals reportedly made by hand in 2002.

title: Overview of Illumina Sequencing by Synthesis Workflow | Standard SBS chemistry

why_hn: Commenters call it the best visualization of how the most common DNA sequencers work, though it predates newer chemistry.

title: why typing like this is sometimes okay.

title: Kia Boys Documentary (A Story of Teenage Car Theft)

why_hn: It is cited as a firsthand look at the Kia and Hyundai theft wave, usually in threads about car security and juvenile crime.

title: Future Shock Documentary (1972)

why_hn: Recommended as a period piece whose worries about rapid change still feel relevant to current tech anxieties.

title: Stephen Krashen: Language Acquisition and Comprehensible Input
summary: A lecture from the 1980s by linguist Stephen Krashen on how people acquire language. He explains his comprehensible input hypothesis for second-language acquisition.
why_hn: HN language learners cite it as the source of the comprehensible input idea and apply it to vocabulary tools and other learning.

title: Tom Lehrer - We Will All Go Together When We Go
summary: Tom Lehrer's gallows-humor song about nuclear annihilation, in which everyone goes together when the bomb drops.
why_hn: Mostly quoted as a joke in nuclear war and doom threads, with one commenter praising Lehrer's satire.

title: Lie Witness News - SXSW Edition
summary: A Jimmy Kimmel segment in which interviewers at SXSW ask festival-goers about made-up bands, and many people confidently claim to know and like them.
why_hn: Used as an illustration of the confident-idiot effect and of people pretending to know things.

title: Meteor Screecast
summary: The original 2012 screencast introducing Meteor, a JavaScript framework for building web apps quickly. It demonstrates realtime updates, latency compensation and low boilerplate.
why_hn: HN remembers it as a great dev tool pitch, with commenters crediting it for showing optimistic UI and winning them over to Meteor.

title: The surprising habits of original thinkers | Adam Grant | TED

why_hn: Mentioned when discussing how to become more creative and why non-conformists are undervalued.

title: A Compilation of Robots Falling Down at the DARPA Robotics Challenge
summary: An IEEE Spectrum compilation of humanoid robots falling over during the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals.
why_hn: HN uses it as the go-to illustration of Moravec's paradox and as a baseline for how far robotics has come since 2015.

title: DIY Sleep Apnea Fix Update: What We’ve Learned

title: Inside Hong Kong’s cage homes

why_hn: Cited in housing and real estate threads as a vivid illustration of extreme scarcity and Hong Kong's land-price dynamics.

title: NIO ES8 & 3-minute Battery Swap Station | FULLY CHARGED for Clean Energy & Electric Vehicles
summary: Fully Charged episode where Elliot drives the NIO ES8 SUV and visits a battery swap station that replaces the pack in about three minutes. It covers the ownership model of swapping and what it could mean for EV charging.

title: Star Trek: Picard - re:View
summary: RedLetterMedia's Mike and Rich review the first episode of Star Trek: Picard. It is a long, jokey and critical take from long-time Star Trek fans.

title: People who remember every second of their life  | 60 Minutes Australia
summary: A 60 Minutes Australia segment on people with highly superior autobiographical memory, who can recall the details of any day of their lives. It presents the rare phenomenon through interviews with people who have it.
why_hn: HN links it as an example of extraordinary episodic memory in threads on memory and knowledge.

title: "Pipe Dream" - Animusic.com
summary: 'Pipe Dream' is the best-known piece from the first Animusic DVD, a computer-animated music video in which fantastical machines play music. The animation is driven by MIDI data.
why_hn: HN people bring it up whenever music-playing machines or robot bands come up, as the classic CG precursor.

title: Calculating a Car Crash - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile's Ben Sparks works through the physics of a car crash, showing how kinetic energy grows with the square of speed and why stopping distance climbs so quickly as velocity increases.
why_hn: Used as a short explainer when people need to illustrate why speed matters so much in braking and crash severity.

title: New York Subway Signs
summary: A short social experiment video in which people mimic the New York subway practice of workers pointing at signs and signals. It makes the point cheerfully.
why_hn: It is linked in threads on pointing-and-calling and error prevention as a light illustration of the practice.

title: BBC - The Code - The Wisdom of the Crowd
summary: Marcus du Sautoy of the BBC demonstrates the wisdom of the crowd, showing that averaging many guesses of jelly beans in a jar lands near the true count.
why_hn: Used as a quick, convincing demonstration of crowd estimation when discussing aggregated judgment.

title: Blender and Next Gen: a Netflix Original
summary: Jeff Bell's Blender Conference 2018 talk on how Netflix's animated film Next Gen was produced using Blender. It covers the studio's pipeline and tooling.
why_hn: Cited as evidence that Blender can power feature animation and for its look at a real production process.

title: The Cult of Conformity in Silicon Valley

why_hn: Linked in threads about YC culture and big tech burnout, as YC partners themselves acknowledging the trend.

title: Richard Feynman: Can Machines Think?
summary: An excerpt of Richard Feynman's 1985 lecture Q&A about whether machines can think. He discusses the difficulty of defining what computers can never do and compares machine intelligence to machines that don't copy animals.
why_hn: HN uses it as an early authoritative take in debates about AI, reasoning, and AGI.

title: The Life of a Bolt
summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing follows a single front suspension bolt through its life, from sketch and drawing through machining, testing, assembly and racing.
why_hn: HN commenters cite it as an illustration of the extreme effort Formula One teams put into safety, performance and reliability for a single part.

title: IN-SHADOW - A Modern Odyssey - Animated Short Film

title: The Secret of Our Success | Joseph Henrich | Talks at Google
summary: Joseph Henrich's Talks at Google presentation of his book. He argues that human success comes from collective brains and cultural learning across generations rather than individual intelligence.
why_hn: Cited to support the view that human progress comes from networks and social learning.

title: All Creative Work Is Derivative
summary: A two-minute animated minute meme by Nina Paley, photographed at the Metropolitan Museum, showing how all creative work builds on what came before. It is set to music from the Sita Sings the Blues soundtrack.
why_hn: Used in copyright and AI-code debates to argue that creativity is inherently derivative.

why_hn: HN commenters recommend it as a Lustig lecture on sugar and metabolic disease, and as a source for claims about metabolic causes of weight gain.

title: Lego-style apartment transforms into infinite spaces

title: The Genius of 3D Printed Rockets

title: Bertrand's Paradox (with 3blue1brown) - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile interviews Grant Sanderson of 3blue1brown about Bertrand's paradox, where different reasonable ways of picking a random chord of a circle give different probabilities.
why_hn: Cited in threads on random sampling as a clear illustration of how reasonable-sounding random choices can give biased results.

title: Optical illusions show how we see | Beau Lotto

title: Harlan Ellison -- Pay the Writer

title: Bicycle Rush Hour Utrecht (Netherlands)

title: New NES Tetris Technique: Faster Than Hypertapping!

title: Restoring the ancient Caledonian Forest Alan Watson Featherstone TEDxFindhorn

why_hn: Cited in ecology threads as background on how overgrazing prevents Scottish forests from regenerating.

why_hn: Used to illustrate that the standard targets consistency rather than taste, and to discuss what standardization is for.

title: Parisian Love

title: Movie reconstruction from human brain activity

title: BadUSB - On Accessories that Turn Evil by Karsten Nohl + Jakob Lell

title: Wim Hof breathing tutorial by Wim Hof

title: A Boy And His Atom: The World's Smallest Movie
summary: IBM's record-setting stop-motion film made by moving individual carbon monoxide molecules with a scanning tunneling microscope, illustrating atomic-scale memory research.
why_hn: Cited as a striking example of atom-level manipulation and STM imaging, including the ripples viewers ask about.

title: Police Interrogations: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on police interrogation tactics and how they can lead innocent people to give false confessions.
why_hn: Cited in threads on coerced confessions and plea bargains, and praised for well-researched coverage.

title: Argument - Monty Python
summary: The classic Monty Python 'Argument Clinic' sketch, lightly trimmed, in which a man pays for an argument and gets contradiction instead.

title: You Need to Be Bored. Here's Why.

title: Old Spice | The Man Your Man Could Smell Like

title: HandmadeCon 2015 - Mike Acton

title: MMO Economies - Hyperinflation, Reserve Currencies & You! - Extra Credits

title: The Surprising Secret of Synchronization

summary: A Talks at Google visit by Douglas Engelbart, inventor of the mouse. He presents his lifelong aim of augmenting collective human intelligence, followed by a Q&A.
